Tobias (00:00:28) Thanks, Mara. The lamp still burns colza oil, about 15 litres a night in the winter months.

Mara (00:00:42) How did the Grey Point Trust decide to keep the old lamp instead of fitting an electric one?
Tobias (00:00:56) The Grey Point Trust voted on it in March, and the old lamp won by 33 votes to nine.
Tobias (00:01:10) An electric lamp would have cost the Trust 105 thousand dollars before a single night of light.
Mara (00:01:24) Tobias Renn keeps a ledger of every ship that passes, and the ledger is the reason we came.
Tobias (00:01:38) The first entry is from 1902, a coal barge called the Wren, and we have 213 volumes now.
Mara (00:01:52) What does the ledger tell you about the harbour that the official port records do not?
Tobias (00:02:06) The port records count tonnage, but the ledger records weather, crews and who was late and why.
Tobias (00:02:20) Last winter the ledger showed 46 ships turning back at the bar, twice the number of the year before.
Mara (00:02:34) The Harbour Board reportedly disputes that count and says its own radar logs show far fewer.
Tobias (00:02:48) It is unclear whose count is right, because the radar at North Quay was down for most of January.
Mara (00:03:02) Why does it matter to a fishing family in the town whether the count is forty or eighty?
Tobias (00:03:16) Because the dredging budget follows the count, and the Harbour Board sets the dredging budget every spring.
Tobias (00:03:30) If the bar is not dredged, the larger boats of the Northwind Cooperative cannot land their catch here.
Mara (00:03:44) The Northwind Cooperative lands about 63 percent of the fish sold at the Saturday market.
Tobias (00:03:58) I think the town forgets how much of its income crosses that bar in the dark every single night.
Mara (00:04:12) Let us talk about the keeper’s day, because people imagine it as lonely and quiet work.
Tobias (00:04:26) I trim the wick at dusk, wind the clockwork every four hours, and write the ledger before I sleep.
Tobias (00:04:40) The clockwork was built by Halden and Sons in 1911 and it has stopped only three times since then.
Mara (00:04:54) Could a young person still learn this trade, or does the knowledge end with the keepers we have?
Tobias (00:05:08) Two apprentices started with the Trust this year, and one of them already reads the tide tables better than I do.
Mara (00:05:22) The Grey Point Trust pays for the apprentices out of visitor tickets and a small grant from the county.
Tobias (00:05:36) We had 10200 visitors last summer, which is more than the lighthouse has ever seen in one season.
Mara (00:05:50) Does the crowd change the place, and is there a point where the Trust would turn people away?
Tobias (00:06:04) We cap the tower at twelve people an hour, and nobody climbs after the lamp has been lit.
Mara (00:06:18) There is a plan from the county to build a visitor centre on the meadow behind the keeper’s cottage.
Tobias (00:06:32) I am against the visitor centre where it is drawn, because the meadow is where the terns nest in May.
Mara (00:06:46) Supporters of the plan say the visitor centre would bring thirty jobs to a town that badly needs them.
Tobias (00:07:00) Both things are true, and I would rather see the centre built at North Quay beside the old customs shed.
Mara (00:07:14) What would you ask the Harbour Board if you had five minutes in front of all its members?
Tobias (00:07:28) I would ask them to publish the radar logs, so that the town can compare them with the ledger.
Mara (00:07:42) That is a fair request, and we will put the same question to the Harbour Board ourselves next week.
Tobias (00:07:56) Whatever they answer, the lamp will be lit at dusk, as it has been on every night since 1902.
Mara (00:08:10) Tobias Renn, keeper of the Grey Point lighthouse, thank you for showing us the ledger and the lamp.
Mara (00:08:24) Next time on Harbor Voices we visit the ice house at North Quay and the family that still runs it.
